mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 3% over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 3% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below 900K signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 900K in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase of 0.4 percentage points or more over two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp in two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) after such UNRATE increases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, which is expected to drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both GDPC1 and RSAFS decline month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) cut of at least 0.5 percentage points in a single meeting, in the context of a recession (UNRATE > 6%), signals aggressive monetary easing that boosts risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) after such easing episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 alongside a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) suggests a paradoxical labor market, indicating structural shifts that typically precede equity market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during such paradoxical labor market signals.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between the trajectory of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, such that a month-over-month CPI increase above 0.3% predicts positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: The correlation between monthly CPI > 0.3% and positive 5-day S&P 500 returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample testing.
